| Edge | Condition (source, verbatim) | Bearing document (blocked problem = payoff) | Strength | Restated in the depended-on problem's docs? |

| payoff -> returned_fee_waiver (value_input, gate fees_due) | "Every returned payment fee that followed an autopay debit presented to a closed source account has been waived before the payoff amount is fixed." | payoff_ledger_balances, "Entry condition for the fees due" (verbatim) + "Where that does not yet hold, the payoff amount is not fixed." | same: the source "Before the payoff amount is fixed, ... is waived" is a pre-condition on fixing the amount; the KB's added sentence is its contrapositive | no: returned_fee_* and returned_payment_fee_bank_error_waiver do not mention the payoff |
| payoff -> late_charge_waiver (value_input, gate fees_due) | "Every late charge on an installment left unpaid by an autopay debit presented to a closed source account has been waived before the payoff amount is fixed." | same_day_payoff Policy 3 "Entry condition" (verbatim) + "Where that does not yet hold, the payoff amount is not fixed." | same | no: late_charge_* and late_charge_bank_error_waiver do not mention the payoff |
policy_source homes: both rule sentences ("Before the payoff amount is fixed, every ... is waived for bank error under its own rule") are carried by the two entry conditions above; "for bank error under its own rule" is not repeated there, but the fee each condition describes ("followed an autopay debit presented to a closed source account") is by definition the one the bank-error rule waives, so the meaning is unchanged. The `effect` of the returned-fee edge ("fees_due falls ... and the payoff amount falls by the same amount") appears as payoff_ledger_balances "Because fee waivers are taken off, a fee waived before the payoff amount is fixed lowers the fees due, and so lowers the payoff amount, by the fee waived" — a derivation of the fees-due formula, naming no tool.
